A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching methodology and core experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama-2 neuron-deactivation experiments, multilingual evaluations, fact-frequency analysis, and concept-neuron analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Gemma-7B experiments, prompt-template controls, perplexity measurements, and error analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions identify neurons through token-averaged activations, average-precision ranking against counter-relation examples, and zeroing selected neurons during inference. RelSpec is new terminology; the additional evaluations do not establish a changed identification or intervention procedure.

E1.justification: The 12 LRE relations, six languages, and Dolma analysis are retained. Coverage expands through alternative English templates for the same held-out triples and synthetic object-containing sentences outside the original factual queries, adding limited input scenarios and a language-modeling task.

E2.justification: The original-model and random-neuron-deactivation comparators remain, as do the neuron-module variants and concept-neuron comparisons. Gemma-7B uses the same comparator types; no new competing identification method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design: Gemma-7B experiments, intermediate-block ablations across eight consecutive threshold pairs, perplexity measurements on 4–50 synthetic sentences per relation, and 20-token error illustrations. The original 50-triple holdouts and two-token factual-recall evaluation remain.

E4.justification: The single 1,000-versus-3,000-neuron cumulativity check becomes a systematic range analysis in Figure 6 and Table 3. New analyses address template dependence, general language-modeling disruption, generated-error patterns, and robustness across model families. The earlier multilingual, frequency, and neuron-type analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the main random-deactivation baseline over ten seeds, qualitative stability under negative-sampling seeds, and the same Wilcoxon test with p-values 0.11 and 0.03. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice; macro/micro cumulativity averages are metric aggregation.

E6.justification: Core Llama-2 results, including Figure 4 and the original cumulativity table entries, are retained. v2 adds substantial Gemma, template-transfer, cumulativity, perplexity, and error results. For example, its new Table 2 reports ablation perplexity changing from 62.71 to 84.31 for person_occupation. Concept-overlap displays omit food, pokemon, and superhero entries and revise non-overlap counts, while concept validation retains all eleven concepts.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition of cumulativity as 1 minus #affected/#total, with macro and micro aggregation. v1 reports the underlying counts without this metric. Existing identification and accuracy-drop mathematics remain substantively unchanged, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims of relation-specific neurons, versatility, and interference remain. Cumulativity is strengthened from increasing factual degradation as more neurons are disabled to joint processing with no single neuron fully encoding a fact, explicitly stated in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments separating relation semantics from prompt syntax and general object-generation ability, plus interpretations of post-ablation errors. Appendix B discusses object-distribution imbalance, and the limitations expand to model-family and post-training generalization. The earlier distinct-object-count explanation for sensitivity is removed; the fact-frequency explanation remains.

D1.justification: The release statement changes from planned code availability to stated public code-and-data availability. Appendix K documents the new paraphrase and synthetic-sentence templates. Hardware and Python-environment disclosures remain unchanged; actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 connects neuron versatility to polysemanticity and superposition, adding Mu and Andreas, Elhage's superposition work, and Scherlis et al. It also cites Gemma and Sclar et al. for the added experiments. The broader related-work survey and statistics-based positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes RelSpec terminology, revises explanatory passages and footnotes, and moves the fact-frequency analysis from Section 5.3 to Appendix E. Supplementary sections are reorganized, but the main narrative framework and much of the existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds displays for Gemma, cumulativity, prompt transfer, perplexity, and errors, and greatly expands the cumulativity table. Existing multilingual plots replace mirrored bars with bars and horizontal markers; sensitivity plots gain percentage annotations, and concept-overlap heatmaps are transposed and reduced. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The template-transfer and language-modeling controls test important alternative explanations left untested in v1. Expanded cumulativity validation and Gemma replication further strengthen the central empirical evidence. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: Section 5.4 says nine concepts while overlap figures show eight and appendix validation retains eleven, and the stronger single-neuron claim exceeds what the group ablations establish.
